source_name: Register partnerov verejného sektora (RPVS) — Ministerstvo spravodlivosti SR
why_relevant: Public UBO/beneficial-ownership register for entities transacting with the state, flagging whether a UBO is a public official — a practical KYC/PEP data source for SK banks and a proxy for beneficial-ownership transparency quality that MONEYVAL scores. Registration is mediated by oprávnené osoby including banks.

source_name: SKDP (Slovenská komora daňových poradcov) — AML legislative commentary and consultation alerts
why_relevant: Professional-chamber commentary that reliably names the underlying legislative identifiers (e.g. novela 73/2026 Z. z., LP/2025/518, PI/2026/51) and circulates consultation calls on the AML strategy and NRA — an efficient pointer layer for finding official documents fast.

source_name: SK law-firm and compliance AML trackers (Škubla & Partneri, Semančín, aml-cft.sk)
why_relevant: Practitioner blogs summarising SK AML amendments, FSJ inspection practice and fine levels, and NRA outcomes; useful for early detection and for surfacing FSJ documents that are hard to find via site navigation. Secondary — always verify against FSJ/NBS/Slov-Lex.

source_name: NBS – Ochrana finančného spotrebiteľa (OFS) hub, consumer section
why_relevant: Top node of the NBS financial-consumer-protection arm; branches into consumer information, professional-public information (guidance, consultations), complaint handling and activity reports. Best single entry point for snowballing the whole conduct-supervision sub-tree.

source_name: NBS – Riešenie sťažností / complaint handling for financial consumers
why_relevant: Describes NBS as single contact point for complaints against all supervised institutions, plus procedure and notices (oznamy). Complaint intake rules and any changes to them affect the volume/visibility of conduct weak signals.

source_name: NBS – Správa o činnosti útvaru dohľadu v oblasti ochrany finančného spotrebiteľa (annual OFS activity report)
why_relevant: Annual report series (reported for 2019-2024) with statistics on consumer submissions, inspection themes and sanctions. Best quantified time series of conduct pressure by product and by institution type; useful for trend and thematic-priority detection.

source_name: Úrad na ochranu osobných údajov SR (Slovak DPA) – official site
why_relevant: The supervisory authority for GDPR in Slovakia; its site structure exposes Legislatíva a judikatúra, Metodiky a FAQ, Kontrola spracúvania osobných údajov (including an annual inspection plan), and news items covering CJEU/EDPB outcomes. Directly governs banks' data processing, biometrics/KYC, marketing consent and profiling.

source_name: ÚOOÚ – Plán kontrol (annual data-protection inspection plan)
why_relevant: Forward-looking statement of which sectors and processing operations the DPA will inspect in the coming year. A leading indicator: if banking/fintech/credit-scoring appears, enforcement pressure follows within 12-24 months. Path pattern suggests a per-year page series.

source_name: ÚOOÚ – Správa o stave ochrany osobných údajov (annual report to Parliament)
why_relevant: Annual PDF series (2021-2024 confirmed) with statistics on complaints, inspections, fines and thematic issues; the practical substitute for a fully public decision database. Stable filename pattern under /files/annual-reports/.

source_name: ÚOOÚ – Legislatíva a judikatúra / Metodiky a FAQ
why_relevant: The DPA's soft-law layer: methodologies, short ad-hoc methodical notes and FAQ, plus a case-law section carrying CJEU/national rulings the office considers relevant. Interpretive positions here shape bank compliance projects before any fine appears.

source_name: SOI – Slovenská obchodná inšpekcia, právoplatné rozhodnutia (first- and second-instance decisions)
why_relevant: SOI publishes final decisions as regional-year-indexed PDFs. Although financial services are largely carved out to NBS, SOI still reaches general consumer-protection breaches (unfair/misleading practices, contract terms, information duties, distance selling) by traders including leasing, credit intermediation and ancillary retail-finance offers, and files ARS/collective actions.

source_name: SOI – Výročná správa (annual report)
why_relevant: Annual account of inspection volumes, thematic campaigns, sanctions and ARS caseload; identifies which consumer sectors (incl. credit/leasing/e-commerce payments) were prioritised. Stable /files/documents/kcinnost/{year}/ pattern.

source_name: SOI – Alternatívne riešenie spotrebiteľských sporov (ARS rules and residual ADR body)
why_relevant: SOI is the residual ADR entity under Act 391/2015; its ARS rules page and caseload show how out-of-court consumer disputes (including some financial ones falling outside sectoral ADR) are handled, and expose procedural deadlines for traders.

source_name: MH SR – Zoznam subjektov alternatívneho riešenia spotrebiteľských sporov (official ADR-body register)
why_relevant: Authoritative register of ADR entities, which is how you enumerate every ombudsman-type dispute body competent for financial services in SK (e.g. the Slovak Banking Association's ARS institute, registered 7 April 2016). Also links the European Commission consolidated ADR list.

source_name: Inštitút alternatívneho riešenia sporov Slovenskej bankovej asociácie (ARS SBA) – banking ombudsman-type body
why_relevant: The sector ADR body for banking disputes, registered by MH SR since April 2016. Its rules, scope, member banks and any published outcomes/statistics are the closest thing SK has to a banking ombudsman and are a strong weak-signal channel on retail-banking practice disputes.

source_name: OMBUDSPOT – združenie na ochranu práv spotrebiteľov (registered ADR entity)
why_relevant: One of the registered non-state ADR entities handling consumer disputes including financial-services complaints; NGOs like this surface complaint patterns and litigate/publicise practices before regulators act.

source_name: Spoločnosť ochrany spotrebiteľov (S.O.S.) – consumer NGO with financial-services focus
why_relevant: Explicitly focuses on enforcing rights of consumer groups harmed by providers in energy, telecoms and FINANCIAL services and digital rights, and runs advisory centres on unfair/misleading commercial practices and unacceptable contract terms. Their campaigns and case write-ups are early indicators of mis-selling themes.

source_name: MH SR – Príloha: Spotrebiteľské organizácie a zameranie ich činnosti (register of consumer organisations)
why_relevant: Ministry-compiled list of Slovak consumer organisations and their thematic focus — the fastest way to enumerate the NGO layer (ZSS, S.O.S., OMBUDSPOT and others) that generates conduct weak signals and represents consumers in court.

source_name: Fininfo.sk – Ministerstvo financií SR financial-consumer portal
why_relevant: MF SR's consumer-facing portal maps the institutional division of labour (MF SR vs NBS vs ADR bodies) and hosts the 'kam sa obrátiť s problémom' / mimosúdne riešenie sporu pages. Useful as a canonical actor map and to detect MF SR policy framing ahead of legislation (e.g. CCD2 transposition).

source_name: MH SR – Ochrana spotrebiteľa / ARS section (consumer-policy owner)
why_relevant: Ministry of Economy owns horizontal consumer-protection policy and Act 391/2015 on ADR; its pages carry policy changes, FAQ and the legal framework that also binds financial-service traders where NBS's sectoral regime does not displace it.

source_name: MH SR – Prebiehajúce konzultácie a predbežné informácie (business-impact consultations)
why_relevant: Pre-legislative consultations under the Jednotná metodika (RIA) framework, where consumer-protection and financial-conduct drafts surface with impact assessments and deadlines before they reach Slov-Lex. Complements NBS's own consultation channel.

source_name: Spolok pre ochranu osobných údajov (SOOÚ) – DPA case commentary
why_relevant: Specialist association that publishes analyses of ÚOOÚ decisions, including a banking case (mBank, Art. 13 GDPR information-duty breach in branches, remediated from 13 May 2019). Because the Slovak DPA does not run a comprehensive public decision database, such commentary is often the only way to see decision texts and reasoning.

source_name: Law-firm and compliance trackers on Slovak GDPR enforcement (Havel & Partners, Dagital Legal, Podnikajte.sk, i-secure)
why_relevant: Practitioner aggregations of ÚOOÚ fining patterns, fine ceilings and procedural problems of the authority. Useful to reconstruct enforcement trends that the authority itself does not publish case-by-case, and to spot capacity/backlog issues that delay decisions.

source_name: Slovak legal/consumer-finance commentary on new Consumer Credit Act (zákon č. 312/2025 Z. z., CCD2 transposition)
why_relevant: Tracks the single biggest live conduct-regulation change for SK retail banking — the new consumer-credit law transposing CCD2, effective from 2026 — including creditworthiness, disclosure and total-cost rules that drive NBS supervisory priorities and deadlines.

source_name: NRSR – parliamentary document preview (tabled supervisory/DPA reports and consumer bills)
why_relevant: The Slovak Parliament hosts tabled versions of the DPA's annual report and of NBS/consumer-protection materials, sometimes with committee positions and dates. A useful mirror when agency sites reorganise, and a place where political pressure on conduct supervision becomes visible.

source_name: European Commission – consolidated list of ADR/dispute-resolution bodies (SK filter)
why_relevant: EU-level cross-check on which Slovak ombudsman-type bodies are notified as competent for financial services; catches bodies missing from or lagging in the national register and supports comparison with other member states.

source_name: NBS – Pravidlá platobného systému SIPS (SIPS payment system rules)
source_subtype: central bank payment system rulebook page
why_relevant: Authoritative rules of the Slovak domestic interbank payment system SIPS/EURO SIPS operated by NBS: participation contract, message formats, operating timetable (časový harmonogram) and fee schedule (sadzobník). Changes here are binding operational deadlines for every SK participant.

source_name: NBS – Platobné systémy / TARGET Services (T2, T2S, TIPS) section
why_relevant: NBS pages on T2/T2S consolidation, TARGET-SK and TIPS describe Slovak participation conditions, DCA/TIPS account rules and migration milestones for SK banks and (since Oct 2025) non-bank PSPs.

source_name: NBS decisions/rozhodnutia on payment system participation (e.g. rozhodnutie NBS č. 10/2022, 9/2018, 4/2010)
why_relevant: NBS decisions are the legally binding instrument setting harmonised participation conditions for TARGET2-SK/TARGET-SK, TIPS DCAs and ancillary-system settlement — the hard rule layer beneath the descriptive web pages.
